name: Paytm
summary: Candidates commonly report that Paytm's engineering interviews include an online coding test, two or more technical rounds on problem-solving, design and past projects, and a final round with a hiring manager or HR. Questions often draw on its payments and merchant business, such as QR payments, payment speakers for shops and transaction reliability. Paytm describes a culture of entrepreneurship, executing with speed and thinking big.
rounds: Online coding and aptitude test (for many engineering and campus roles)
Technical interviews on data structures, problem-solving and core subjects, often two or more
Design round on a system or a past project (for experienced roles)
looks_for: Correctness and reliability when money is involved

questions.text: Tell me about a time you made a big decision quickly and then owned the result.
covers: Why the decision couldn't wait
What you knew, what you didn't, and the risk you accepted
How it turned out, and what you did when parts of it went wrong

questions.text: Tell me about an idea you suggested or built outside your assigned work. What happened to it?
covers: The problem you noticed and why it mattered
How you built or pitched it alongside your main work
Who used it or what happened next, even if it didn't go ahead

questions.text: Describe a time you worked with a non-engineering team, such as sales or operations, to solve a customer problem.
covers: The customer problem and what each team saw of it
How you understood their side and agreed on a fix
The result for the customer

questions.text: Tell me about something you built that failed in production. What did you learn?
covers: What failed and who it affected, owned plainly
How you found the cause and fixed it
What you now do differently when building or testing

questions.text: How would you design the backend for a shop's payment speaker that announces each payment as it arrives?
covers: The event flow from payment success to the device, over a lasting connection
Devices that go offline, and making sure a payment is announced once, not missed or repeated
Security: only real payments trigger it, and each device is authenticated

questions.text: Walk me through a QR code payment at a small shop, from scan to the shopkeeper seeing it. What can go wrong?
covers: Static versus dynamic QR codes, and the path through the payer's app, UPI and the banks
Pending payments, timeouts and refunds
How the shopkeeper is told, and how their records are reconciled

questions.text: Explain database transactions and isolation levels. Where could a weak isolation level hurt a wallet balance?
covers: What ACID means, in plain words
The common isolation levels and what each allows
A lost update or double spend, and how locks or version checks prevent it

questions.text: A customer's money was debited but their order shows as failed. How would you design the system to sort out cases like this?
covers: A clear pending state, and checking the final status with the bank
Automatic completion or refund within a set time, without doing both
Telling the customer what is happening, and an audit trail of every step

questions.text: How would you protect a payments API from abuse, such as stolen logins or repeated failed attempts?
covers: Rate limits, device binding and a second factor such as an OTP
Rules or models that flag unusual behaviour
Logging and alerts, and error messages that don't help an attacker

questions.text: How would you get more small shopkeepers in a town to accept digital payments, and how would you measure it?
covers: Their barriers: trust, fees, set-up effort, waiting for settlement
How you'd reach them: field teams, simple onboarding, a device that confirms payments
Metrics: active merchants, payments per merchant, and how many are still using it later

questions.text: Explain the difference between a process and a thread, with an example from an app you've built.
covers: Processes have separate memory; threads share memory within one process
Why that makes threads cheaper but brings race conditions
A real example: a background job, a web server or a mobile app's main thread

questions.text: Why Paytm? Which part of its business would you like to work on?
covers: Something specific: consumer payments, merchant products or financial services
What you know of its users and their problems
How your skills fit that area

questions.text: Are you comfortable in a fast-moving team where priorities can change from week to week?
covers: An honest yes, with a past example of priorities changing
How you keep track of what matters most when they change
What you need from a manager to work well that way

questions.text: What would you want to have learned or built after your first six months here?
covers: One or two concrete goals tied to the role
The skills you want to build
How you'd know you were on track

tips: Use Paytm before the interview as a customer and look at what a merchant sees, such as payment confirmations; product examples help.
Payments questions reward care: cover pending states, duplicate requests, refunds and reconciliation, not only the happy path.
For campus roles, revise core subjects (operating systems, databases, networks) as well as data structures; they often come up.
Paytm says ideas can come from anyone and that some of its features began as weekend projects; a side project you can explain in depth is worth bringing up.
When you talk about speed, show how you also protect customers' money: tests, gradual rollouts and quick rollbacks.
